title: Karan Johar Credits Shah Rukh Khan and Aditya Chopra for His Career on Guru Purnima
excerpt: The filmmaker shared an emotional Instagram tribute recalling two life-changing conversations — a 1 AM phone call from Chopra and a hilltop promise from Khan — that launched his three-decade career in Hindi cinema.
body:
• Karan Johar posted an emotional Instagram tribute on Guru Purnima (July 29) thanking Shah Rukh Khan and Aditya Chopra as the two people responsible for his filmmaking career.
  • He recalled a late-night phone call from Aditya Chopra that pulled him away from plans to study abroad and onto the set of Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge (1995).
  • Shah Rukh Khan promised on a hilltop in Switzerland to star in Johar's directorial debut — a pledge he kept with Kuch Kuch Hota Hai (1998).
  • Johar's post resonated across Indian cinema circles on a day traditionally devoted to honouring mentors and teachers.

Filmmaker Karan Johar marked Guru Purnima on July 29 with a lengthy Instagram post and a collage of photographs alongside Shah Rukh Khan and Aditya Chopra, calling the two men "the only reason I can tell stories today." The tribute centred on two conversations Johar described as having permanently altered the course of his life — one that kept him in Mumbai, and another that put him behind the camera.

The 1 AM Phone Call That Stopped Him from Leaving

Johar revealed that before he ever stepped foot on a film set, he was preparing to leave India for further studies. That plan unravelled late one night when Aditya Chopra called him at around 1 AM and asked him to come on board as an assistant director on Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge.

Chopra did more than offer a job. He told the young Johar that filmmaking was his calling.

"He told me I had to be a director. I was melodramatic and filmy. He said if I didn't pursue this path, I would be making a huge mistake."

— Karan Johar, via Instagram

Unable to sleep after that conversation, Johar went to his father the next morning. The late producer Yash Johar listened to his son's plea for "a year of his life" on a film set. His response cut through the melodrama: "Beta, will you know what to do on a set?" The elder Johar then drew a line that stayed with his son — following instructions could make him a producer, but becoming a director required "only and only passion."

At that moment, only Aditya Chopra believed Johar had it. "Passionate I was but wasn't sure anyone would believe me at that point," he wrote. "Only Adi did… only him."

A Promise on a Swiss Hilltop

The second conversation happened thousands of miles from Mumbai. While in Switzerland, Shah Rukh Khan stood on a hilltop and casually told Johar that he would become a director — and that Khan himself would star in his first film.

Johar dismissed it at the time, attributing the declaration to mountain air. But Khan was serious. After they returned to India, the actor followed up directly with Yash Johar, who himself wasn't entirely convinced. Khan's conviction held. He went on to headline Kuch Kuch Hota Hai in 1998, Johar's directorial debut, which became one of the biggest Bollywood hits of the decade and launched Johar as a major filmmaking voice.

"He was serious and followed up with my father as we got back to India. My father wasn't sure either," Johar recalled, according to Pinkvilla. Three decades later, Johar still finds it difficult to fully explain why Khan placed so much trust in someone who hadn't yet proven himself.

The Guru Purnima Tradition

Guru Purnima is the Hindu festival dedicated to honouring teachers, mentors, and spiritual guides. Across Bollywood, the day has become an annual occasion for public tributes — this year, stars from Karisma Kapoor to Geeta Kapur also posted messages honouring the people who shaped their careers. But Johar's post stood apart for the specificity and vulnerability of the stories it shared.

"I love you Adi and Bhai. I am here with my strengths and flaws, my ups and downs, my wins and my losses. Only and only because of the both of you."

— Karan Johar, via Instagram

He closed the post with a broader shout-out to "every guru who paid it forward" and helped build careers selflessly — a nod that extended his gratitude beyond the two men he named.

Why This Resonates Beyond Bollywood

The Johar-Khan-Chopra relationship is one of the most storied in Hindi cinema. Aditya Chopra, who directed DDLJ at 23, is now the head of Yash Raj Films, India's largest production house. Shah Rukh Khan remains among the most recognised Indian actors globally. And Johar, through Dharma Productions, has shaped the romantic drama genre for a generation of moviegoers worldwide.

For the Indian diaspora, these three names carry an emotional weight that goes well beyond box-office numbers. Films like DDLJ, Kuch Kuch Hota Hai, and Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham became cultural touchstones in NRI households — weekend Blockbuster rentals, community screenings, and wedding playlists. Johar's tribute is a reminder that the creative ecosystem behind those films was itself built on personal faith and late-night phone calls, not studio machinery.

Looking Ahead

Johar continues to operate as one of Hindi cinema's most prolific producers through Dharma Productions and remains a prominent presence across Indian entertainment. While his post was personal rather than professional, the public nature of the tribute — and the engagement it drew — underscores how deeply audiences still connect with the behind-the-scenes bonds that built Bollywood's modern era. As the industry enters a period of rapid change, with streaming reshaping distribution and new filmmakers bypassing traditional mentorship paths, Johar's Guru Purnima message reads as both a personal thank-you and a quiet argument for the value of being believed in before you've earned it.
